title: Fans become participants
paragraphs: Global fandom is not merely a measurement of attention. Fans organize communities, circulate translations, debate meanings, create derivative art, attend events, buy products, and sometimes engage in public advocacy. These activities can strengthen the durability of a cultural phenomenon after the release of any particular work.

At the same time, fan communities are diverse. Their experiences differ by language, country, age, economic resources, and access to platforms. International popularity does not erase inequalities in visibility or distribution. A global chart position and a local community gathering describe different dimensions of the same broader system.

Cultural exchange also runs in multiple directions. International audiences reinterpret Korean works through their own experiences, while Korean producers encounter foreign trends and collaborative possibilities. The history of Hallyu is thus part of a larger history of globalization, rather than proof of a self-contained cultural origin.
